TMA Analysis for Polymers
Polymers undergo changes in their thermomechanical properties during heating and cooling. TMA analyses can give insights into molecular orientation and quenching effects during cooling. It allows the design of adhesives and other hybrid joints and quality control of shrink films. What is the EN 13501 standard?
EN 13501 is the European standard for fire-classifying construction products and building elements.
As part of the EU’s harmonized approach to fire safety, it is used across all EU member states (and many associated countries) to determine how materials and building components behave in a fire. Materials are categorized into different classes (A1 to F) based on their reaction to fire, smoke production, and flaming droplet production. This classification system helps determine the suitability of materials for various building applications. EN 13501 is divided into several parts, each covering a different type of fire performance classification:
EN 13501-1: Reaction to Fire
This part classifies how construction products (including floorings) contribute to the development of a fire.
Common classes: A1, A2, B, C, D, E, and F (A1 is non-combustible and F indicates that no performance has been determined). It also includes smoke production (s1, s2, s3) and flaming droplets/particles (d0, d1, d2).
EN 13501-2: Fire Resistance
This part classifies the fire resistance of building elements (e.g., walls, doors, floors, and beams) based on how long they maintain their integrity, insulation properties, and/or load-bearing capacity.
EN 13501-3: This part classifies the fire resistance of service installations (e.g., ducts and fire dampers).
EN 13501-4: This part classifies the fire resistance of smoke control systems.
Why It Matters:
Under the EU Construction Products Regulation (CPR), many construction products must bear a CE marking. This requires verified fire performance data according to EN 13501, which ensures that fire safety classifications are comparable and reliable across all European countries.
Meeting these fire classification requirements is critical in order for architects, builders, and material suppliers to ensure that their materials comply with building codes and can be legally placed on the market.
NETZSCH supports manufacturers and testing laboratories in achieving these certifications with its advanced fire testing instruments. Our devices, including cone calorimeters, SBI (single burning item) testers, and KBT (klein-brenner-test) systems, provide precise, standards-compliant measurements of reaction-to-fire and fire-resistance properties. These instruments enable our customers to generate accurate, repeatable data fully aligned with EN 13501 classification needs. This helps them bring safe, compliant products to market with confidence.
